heroHeadline: FAA FORMALLY GROUNDS STARSHIP PENDING IFT-12 INVESTIGATION — ARTEMIS III CREW REVEAL JUNE 9 (12 DAYS); MOON BASE ~$1B CONTRACTS ANNOUNCED MAY 26
heroSubtitle: May 28: The FAA formally grounded Starship operations pending completion of a SpaceX-led IFT-12 mishap investigation (Booster 19 boostback burn failure, May 22) — confirmed by Bloomberg, Washington Post, and Spaceflight Now. IFT-13 (Ship 40 + Booster 20, FCC window May 29–Nov 29) is blocked from a flight license until corrective actions are approved; earliest launch Q3 2026. The orbital propellant transfer demo — a mandatory NASA Artemis III HLS qualification milestone — has slipped to Q3-Q4 2026 at the earliest. June 9 Artemis III crew reveal is 12 days away: NASA's press-credential RSVP deadline for international media (5 p.m. EDT May 28) passed today; the June 9 announcement at JSC (11 a.m. EDT, NASA+) will be the first time astronaut names are publicly assigned to the redesigned LEO rendezvous/docking test mission targeting late 2027. On May 26, NASA awarded ~$1B in Moon Base contracts: Astrolab ($219M CLV-1 crewed rover), Lunar Outpost ($220M Pegasus LTV), Blue Origin ($188M Blue Moon Mark 1 Endurance lander for rover delivery), and Firefly Aerospace (MoonFall hopping drones). Moon Base I — Blue Origin to Shackleton Connecting Ridge — targets fall 2026. The Artemis II crew (Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen) are on Day 48 post-splashdown at JSC continuing reconditioning. MSFC is fabricating the Artemis III structural spacer; the sole remaining ICPS is reserved for Artemis IV (first crewed lunar landing, 2028).
